questions.stem: The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in the shell with n = 3 is
questions.explanation: Maximum electrons = 2n^2 = 2(9) = 18.

questions.explanation: The azimuthal quantum number l fixes the sub-shell and hence the shape.

questions.explanation: The product of uncertainties in position and momentum is at least h/4pi.

questions.stem: The number of unpaired electrons in Fe3+ (Z = 26) is
questions.explanation: Fe3+ has the configuration 3d5, giving five unpaired electrons.

questions.stem: Which series of the hydrogen spectrum lies in the visible region?
questions.explanation: Balmer series transitions end at n = 2 and fall in the visible region.

questions.explanation: Six bond pairs around sulphur require sp3d2 hybridisation.

questions.explanation: O2 has bond order (10 - 6)/2 = 2 with two unpaired electrons.

questions.stem: Which of the following molecules has zero dipole moment?
questions.explanation: CO2 is linear and symmetrical, so its bond dipoles cancel.

questions.stem: The number of sigma bonds present in an ethene molecule is
questions.explanation: Four C-H sigma bonds plus one C-C sigma bond gives five.

questions.stem: Among the following, the shortest carbon-carbon bond is present in
questions.explanation: A triple bond is the shortest and strongest carbon-carbon bond.

questions.stem: The number of moles present in 22 g of carbon dioxide is
questions.explanation: Molar mass of CO2 is 44 g, so 22/44 = 0.5 mol.

questions.stem: Molarity of a solution is defined as
options: Moles of solute per kilogram of solvent
Moles of solute per litre of solution
Grams of solute per litre of solvent
Moles of solvent per litre of solution
questions.explanation: Molarity uses the volume of the solution, molality uses the mass of solvent.

questions.stem: The volume occupied by one mole of an ideal gas at STP is
questions.explanation: At 273 K and 1 atm, one mole of an ideal gas occupies 22.4 L.

questions.explanation: This is Avogadro's number.

questions.stem: In a chemical reaction, the limiting reagent is the one that
options: Is present in the largest amount
questions.explanation: The limiting reagent is used up first and therefore fixes the amount of product.

questions.stem: The mass of one mole of water is
questions.explanation: H2O has a molar mass of 2(1) + 16 = 18 g.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a colligative property?
questions.explanation: Colligative properties depend on the number of solute particles, not their nature.

questions.explanation: p = p0 x mole fraction of that component in the solution.

questions.stem: The van't Hoff factor for completely dissociated NaCl in water is
questions.explanation: NaCl gives two ions per formula unit, so i = 2.

questions.explanation: The ebullioscopic constant multiplies molality, not molarity.

questions.stem: According to Henry's law, the solubility of a gas in a liquid at constant temperature is
options: Directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas
Proportional to the square of pressure
questions.explanation: p = KH x mole fraction of the dissolved gas.

questions.stem: An azeotropic mixture is one that
options: Can be separated completely by fractional distillation
Boils at a constant temperature with unchanged composition
questions.explanation: Azeotropes distil without any change in composition.

questions.stem: The unit of the rate constant of a first order reaction is
questions.explanation: For first order kinetics, k has units of reciprocal time.

questions.explanation: One faraday is the charge on one mole of electrons, about 96500 C.

questions.stem: The half life of a first order reaction with rate constant k is
questions.explanation: t(1/2) = ln2 / k = 0.693 / k and is independent of initial concentration.

questions.explanation: The anode is the negative electrode of a galvanic cell where oxidation occurs.
